# Part A: basic Operations

```{r}
#Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements

#B1 Create a data frame students with 8 rows and columns (use stringsAsFactors = FALSE; sex is "M" or "F"):

students <- data.frame (
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B","C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c("78", "85", "92", "67", "74", "88", "95", "59"),
  final = c("82", "79", "96", "71", "80", "91", "93","65"),
  attendance = c("95", "88", "100", "72", "90", "85", "98", "60"),
  stringAsfactors = FALSE
)
```
```{r}
#B2 Display the structure, dimensions, column names, and summary of students.
str (students)
dim (students)
names (students)
summary (students)
```
```{r}
#B3 Add a column average = the mean of midterm and final for each student, rounded to 1 decimal.
students$average <- round(rowMeans(cbind(as.numeric(students$midterm), as.numeric (students$final))), 1)
```
```{r}
#B4 Add a logical column passed that is TRUE when average >= 70 and attendance >= 75
students$passed <- students$average >= 70 &
students$attendance >= 75
students

```
```{r}
#B5 Using ifelse(), add a column standing with these values based on average:
# "Honors" if average >= 90
# "Good" if average >= 75 (and below 90)
# "Needs support" otherwise
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
ifelse (students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))
students
```
```{r}
#B6 Write a function classify(score) that uses an if/else if/ else chain and returns "Distinction" for 85 or above, "Merit" for 70 to 84, "Pass" for 50 to 69, and "Fail" below 50. test it with sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify) and print the result. 
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return ("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70){
    return ("Merit")
} else if (score >= 50) {
  return ("Pass")
} else {
    return ("Fail")
  }
}
sapply (c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)

```
```{r}
 #Part C: rbind() and cbind()

#C1 Create a data frame new_students with two students. Its columns must match the original, including average, passed and standing, computed the same way:
# id 9, Ines, F, section C, midterm 81, final 84, attendance 92
# id 10, Jamal, M, section A, midterm 70, final 68, attendance 80
# Use rbind() to append them to students, saving the result as students_all.
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  gender = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80)
)

new_students$average <- (new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2

new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 75

new_students$standing <- ifelse(
  new_students$average >= 90, "Excellent",
  ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Improvement")
)

missing_cols <- setdiff(names(students), names(new_students))

for (col in missing_cols) {
  new_students[[col]] <- NA
}

new_students <- new_students[, names(students), drop = FALSE]

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)

students_all
```
```{r}
#C2 Create the numeric vector quiz <- c(8,7,10,6,7,9,10,5,8,6). Use the cbind() to attach it to students_all as a column named quiz. Confirm the result is still a data frame with class()
quiz <- c(8,7,10,6,7,9,10,5,8,6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz)
class(students_all)
```
```{r}
#C3 Create the numeric vector quiz <- c(8,7,10,6,7,9,10,5,8,6). use cbind() to attach it to students_all as a column named quiz. Confirm the result is still a data frame with class()
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)
class(students_all)
```
```{r}
#C4 In a comment (2-3 sentences), explain what error rbind() produces if the data frames have different column names, and show the output if you safely catch it with tryCatch()

# Answer: The rbind() function throws an error when attempting to combine data frames with mismatched column names because R requires identical column structure and naming to stack rows. 
# Using tryCatch() intercepts this error, preventing the script from halting and allowing safe handling of the exception. 
# Safe execution example:
tryCatch(
  rbind(df1, df2),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

```
